<reason>Side A persuasively exposed commodity volatility and the historical failure of industrialize-later, but Side B sustained the decisive financing clash: prioritization diverts scarce capital from depleting extraction that needs continuous upgrades, while regional factories still require dollar-priced inputs and sell for local currency. A never fully answered that balance-of-payments and capex problem, and its retreat to cement and cooking oil weakened its larger manufacturing claim. B also answered A's pressure with dual-use infrastructure tied to licenses and adaptable commodity contracts.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's rebuttals on starving the extraction engine: A claimed existing mines would keep earning while new investment went elsewhere, but B showed extraction declines without upgrades, making the proposed bridge self-undermining alongside the hard-currency mismatch.</best_rebuttal>
